title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
abstract: arXiv:2610.40723v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study adaptive UAV sampling for radio environment map (REM) construction from non-Gaussian IoT observations. Integrated nested Laplace approximation(INLA) updates a Mat\'ern GMRF posterior, with waypoints selected by entropy pre-screening and Sherman--Morrison lookahead over the reachable set. We show that the likelihood-induced Skew-Normal correction has a sextic entropy effect, explaining its limited influence on waypoint selection. Across 19 retained ray-traced windows,Random and lawnmower sampling cost a median 18.0\% and 14.0\% more residual NMSE than posterior-informed sampling, equivalently reductions of 15.3\% and 12.3\% when referred to those baselines, while differences among informative rules remain unresolved. Widening the prior shadowing standard deviation from 6.0 to 10.025\,dB improves NMSE and credible-interval coverage, with monotone improvement over a 4--16\,dB sweep on this corpus and no observed turning point, al

translated_title: 物联网网络中无线电环境地图自适应无人机采样的INLA方法：先验宽度主导精度与校准
translated_abstract: 我们研究了从非高斯物联网观测中构建无线电环境地图（REM）的自适应无人机采样问题。集成嵌套拉普拉斯近似（INLA）用于更新Matérn高斯马尔可夫随机场（GMRF）后验，航点通过熵预筛选和基于可达集的Sherman-Morrison前瞻方法进行选择。我们证明似然诱导的偏正态（Skew-Normal）校正具有六次熵效应，这解释了其对航点选择影响有限的原因。在19个保留的射线追踪窗口中，随机采样和割草机式采样相比后验信息采样分别多产生18.0%和14.0%的中位数残余NMSE，即相对于这些基线分别实现了15.3%和12.3%的降低，而各信息式规则之间的差异仍未解决。将先验阴影衰落标准差从6.0 dB拓宽至10.025 dB可改善NMSE和可信区间覆盖率，在该语料库4–16 dB的扫描范围内呈单调改善且未观察到拐点。
tldr: 该论文提出基于INLA更新Matérn GMRF后验的自适应无人机采样方法来构建无线电环境地图，证明后验信息采样显著优于随机与割草机式基线，且增大先验阴影衰落标准差可在4–16 dB范围内单调提升精度与校准。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an adaptive UAV sampling method based on INLA updating a Matérn GMRF posterior for radio environment map construction, showing that posterior-informed sampling significantly outperforms random and lawnmower baselines, and that widening the prior shadowing standard deviation monotonically improves accuracy and calibration over a 4–16 dB range.
